name: Brookfield

summary.text: Brookfield Asset Management is a Toronto-based alternative asset manager. In August 2018 Brookfield took a 99-year lease on 666 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan from Kushner Companies, paying the rent for the full term upfront (reported at $1.1–1.3 billion), which allowed Kushner Companies to pay down the debt from its 2007 purchase of the building for $1.8 billion. The funds came through Brookfield Property Partners, in which the Qatar Investment Authority was a major investor; Brookfield has said Qatari representatives had no involvement in the transaction. Senator Ron Wyden and Rep. Joaquin Castro opened inquiries into whether the deal influenced U.S. policy toward Qatar.

facts.claim: Kushner Companies had bought 666 Fifth Avenue in 2007 for $1.8 billion while Jared Kushner was its chief executive; the building became a financial strain and the Brookfield lease payment helped pay down its debt. Kushner Companies retained ownership of the land.

openQuestions: The site's headline ('a $1.8 billion tower rescued by a 99-year lease from a fund whose second-largest investor was Qatar') is supported by the Senate Finance Committee release and press reports. Reported figures for the upfront payment vary ($1.1bn–$1.3bn).
Whether the deal influenced U.S. policy toward Qatar was the subject of congressional inquiry; no finding was located.
